Hi Emily — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff.

Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Target workload: real-time triage assistant called during clinician workflows (short prompts ~150-400 tokens).
- Concurrency: baseline expected 100 parallel streaming requests during clinic hours, peak bursts up to ~250 concurrent streams for short windows (2-5 minutes).
- Sustained throughput: ~40-60 QPS average depending on region; burst tolerance needed for shift changes.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms end-to-end for the short prompts; p99 under 750ms as a stretch target.
- Streaming: chunked responses with partial tokens required (WebSocket/HTTP2 streaming preferred).

What Redwood proposes for the POC (initial configuration):
1) Connection pool sizing: recommend a pool with 120 concurrent kept-alive connections from your app tier to Redwood Dedicated for the POC (we’ll measure multiplexing behavior).
2) Concurrency guardrail: map 1 streaming connection -> up to 2 parallel request slots depending on prompt length; initial quota: 250 parallel request slots, with bursting policy to 350 for 5-minute windows.
3) Rate limits: token-rate limit at the account level for server-side safety (we propose 2M tokens/day for the POC) and soft QPS cap at 80 for node-level isolation.
4) Telemetry: we’ll turn on token-level cost breakdown and per-request traces for the POC so we can tune pooling and batching.

Attachments: draft ratecard (redwood-draft-ratecard-v2.pdf) with proposed trial pricing and a short note on how we handle concurrency vs. tokens.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to share a short connection-pool sizing calc and a reference doc for multiplexing behavior (Ben: can you drop the calc by end of day tomorrow?).
- Emily/eng to confirm whether streaming will be via WebSocket or HTTP/2 and share an initial traffic shape (5–10 minute CSV) we can use for sizing.
- Redwood to provision a temporary quota bump for the POC (we’ll propose exact numbers once Ben’s calc is in).
- Schedule 30m ops/eng sync next week after we see the traffic sample.

Happy to adjust — if that looks right I’ll create the HubSpot deal and request the tentative quota increase.

Emily, Markus — putting the sizing notes below and attaching a quick calc (conn-sizing-calcs.xlsx). Long version followed by a TL;DR:

TL;DR: For Skyline’s expected shape I recommend starting with a 120-connection pool, request-slot quota of 250, and enable aggressive KV prefix caching plus small-batch merging. That lets you sustain the 40-60 QPS baseline and absorb the 250 concurrent stream bursts with p95 latency headroom.

Details and rationale:
- Connection pooling vs multiplexing: Redwood supports HTTP/2 multiplexing and connection reuse on dedicated endpoints. For WebSocket streaming we prefer one socket per logical long-lived session; each socket can carry multiple streaming call contexts depending on your client behavior. The recommended kept-alive pool size (120) assumes each backend instance will maintain ~8–12 sockets concurrently — adjust by number of app instances.
- Burst handling: Redwood enforces soft quotas via a leaky-bucket on request slots with configurable burst windows. A hard connection cap is only applied when account capacity is exhausted; soft quota allows temporary overage (we proposed 350 for 5 minutes). When soft quota is exceeded we introduce small token throttles with clear 429 semantics (X-Redwood-RateLimit headers).
- Latency impacts: short prompts benefit from KV cache hits — we recommend warmup runs during the first 24h of the POC to populate common prefixes. If you plan to use very short streaming fragments (<50 tokens) we’ll tune the chunk size to avoid per-chunk RPC overhead.
- Observability & fallback: enable per-request trace and sampling at 100% for the first 48h so we can correlate p95 spikes with queueing. For production we can dial sampling back to 5–10%.

Attachments: conn-sizing-calcs.xlsx (simple model showing pool size sensitivity to app instance count and average socket reuse). Also added a link to a short shared doc with examples: https://drive.redwood.com/s/skyline-poc/conn-sizing.
